newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 4.

text.p: The Finance Ministry plans to raise tax rates by more than 60 percent on two kinds of "shochu", a popular domestic liquor, to narrow the gap between taxes on shochu and imported spirits to conform with a ruling by the World Trade Organisation (WTO) that Japan's tax system discriminates against imported liquor. The ministry also plans to cut taxes on whiskey. It hopes to change the tax rates as early as next April.

Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd is expected to increase its consolidated net profit by 16 percent from a year earlier to around 25 billion yen in the business year to March 1997, helped by good performances by its domestic electronics units and its overseas units. However, the forecast is lower than the company's initial prediction of 35 billion yen due to a decline in steel production.

Japan's top cement makers are expected to see improved business in the year to March 1997. Sumitomo Osaka Cement Co Ltd is to return to current profit, while Chichibu Onoda Cement Corp and Nihon Cement Co Ltd should see large operating profits. The projected gains are attributed to cost-cutting and sales of stockholdings.

Three Japanese truck makers are expected to see their pre-tax profits fall in the business year to March 1997, mainly due to poor sales of large-sized trucks and higher overheads. Profits at Isuzu Motors Ltd and Hino Motors Ltd are expected to fall by more than 25 percent. Nissan Diesel Motor Co Ltd's profit is expected to decrease by about five percent due to costs for convertible bond issues.

The number of U.S. vehicles imported into Japan in calendar 1997 is expected to fall for the first time in 12 years, decreasing by 10,000 to a little more than 120,000 units. The number of vehicles produced by Japanese makers in the United States for shipment to Japan is also to fall by a large amount.

Japanese copper smelters, including Nippon Mining & Metals Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Materials Corp, plan to increase domestic copper production capacity by 10 to 20 percent by 2000 to meet expected increases in demand in Southeast Asia and other regions.
